title: The Pesharim
lead: A pesher ("interpretation") is a Qumran commentary that quotes a prophetic text and says what it refers to in the community's own time. The Habakkuk Pesher (1QpHab) is the best preserved, and it reads the Chaldeans as the Kittim, the wicked as the Wicked Priest and the righteous as the Teacher of Righteousness.

sections.b: The Qumran community wrote pesharim on Isaiah, Hosea, Micah, Nahum, Habakkuk, Zephaniah and the Psalms. A pesher quotes a line (the lemma) and says "Its interpretation concerns..." The community believed that the prophets wrote about the last generation, and that their Teacher of Righteousness was given the key to read them (1QpHab 7). The Habakkuk Pesher, copied in the late first century BC, covers Habakkuk 1-2 through 2:20. Its quotations differ in places from the Masoretic Text. Who the Teacher and the Wicked Priest were is unsettled.
